source: Sowden, Pringle, Gabora (2015) The shifting sands of creative thinking: connections to dual process theory
finding: Review paper. Dual-process models split thought into fast automatic and slow effortful processes. Creativity models split idea generation from evaluation. Both creative modes use both process types.
numbers: No numbers; theory review. Published in Thinking & Reasoning 21(1), 40-60.
limits: Abstract page read only this session, not the full text. Proposes, does not test, the shifting idea.
agent_relevance: Generation and evaluation are modes, not fast or slow. A schema should switch mode by code and allow either speed inside each mode.

source: Sowden, Pringle, Gabora (2015) The shifting sands of creative thinking: connections to dual process theory (proposal)
finding: Authors suggest creativity depends on how the mind shifts between generating and evaluating. They propose dual-process research, neuroimaging and chronometric methods to build interventions.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Untested proposal. Needs timing data that LLMs do not give in the same form.
agent_relevance: The shift itself is the object to engineer. In our agent the shift is a program transition, which makes it measurable (count of switches, tokens per mode).

source: Chen & Ding (2023) Probing the creativity of large language models: can models produce divergent semantic association?
finding: Ran the Divergent Association Task (DAT: 10 unrelated nouns, mean GloVe distance) on LLMs. With greedy decoding GPT-4 beat most humans.
numbers: Greedy: GPT-4 DAT 89.1, above 96.1% of humans; GPT-3.5-turbo DAT 80.8, above the human mean. Other open models lower, roughly in line with size. Prompt was zero-shot, same as Olson et al. 2021. Models: gpt-4-0314, GPT-3.5, Vicuna-13B, Oasst-Llama-30B, ChatGLM-6B and others.
limits: Distance metric depends on word frequency. A naive WordNet random sampler also beat most humans and models, so DAT alone is a weak creativity test. Authors say they test 'little-C' only.
agent_relevance: A task of pure remote association is nearly saturated by frontier LLMs. A generate-mode check should not rely on DAT-type scores.

source: Chen & Ding (2023) Probing the creativity of large language models: can models produce divergent semantic association? (temperature, top-p)
finding: Sampling randomness raised DAT for weaker models but made them unstable. GPT-4 did not gain from it.
numbers: Temperature swept 0.1 to 1. Positive effect for all models except GPT-4. Top-p 0.9 with t 0.7 used for sampling runs. Authors: effect 'limited', with unstable and invalid answers at high temperature.
limits: Single task, single word-list format.
agent_relevance: Randomness is a weak, noisy way to get generate mode. Better to switch mode by prompt and structure than by temperature alone.

source: Chen & Ding (2023) Probing the creativity of large language models: can models produce divergent semantic association? (surprisal control)
finding: Controlling for word rarity (surprisal), GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 still beat average human DAT, but GPT-4's lead shrank. Base and Random conditions tested validity.
numbers: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-Turbo exceed the average human DAT at equal surprisal; other models fall short. Appendix D has the controlled numbers (not extracted).
limits: Appendix numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Part of the apparent LLM remote-association skill is rare-word choice. Judge novelty with frequency controlled.

source: Chen & Ding (2023) Probing the creativity of large language models: can models produce divergent semantic association? (dual-process framing)
finding: Cites the dual-process theory of creativity (Beaty et al. 2014): creative thought needs remote association plus inhibition of common ideas. Models' stability under sampling is read as implicit control.
numbers: Qualitative.
quote: According to the dual-process theory of creativity (Beaty et al., 2014)
limits: Framing only. No test of an evaluation or inhibition stage.
agent_relevance: Mode split: associate widely, then suppress common items. This is a code-run filter.

source: Nath, Dayan, Stevenson (2024) Characterising the creative process in humans and large language models
finding: Embedding-based jump profiles of Alternate Uses and Verbal Fluency responses. Humans reach equal creativity by persistent or flexible search. Each LLM leans to one path depending on task.
numbers: Abstract only: no numbers. Flexible LLMs score higher on creativity; in humans both styles score alike.
limits: Abstract page read, not the PDF. Numbers not checked.
agent_relevance: Models do not shift between narrow and broad search as people do; code should force the shift (broaden, then deepen).

source: Chavez (2025) Artificial creativity: from predictive AI to Generative System 3
finding: Conceptual paper. Maps System 1 (spontaneous ideation, default-mode network), System 2 (goal-directed evaluation, central-executive network) and System 3 (metacognitive integrator) onto LLM design. Says LLMs are mostly 'DMN-only decoders' with no evaluator or gain control.
numbers: No data. Proposes a high-entropy generator, a learned critic, and a controller that sets sampling temperature from reward-prediction error.
limits: Paper states it reports no new empirical data. Predictions (drop the critic and usefulness falls; freeze temperature and diversity falls) untested. Brain mapping is analogy. Formulas are in a supplement not read. Last 2000 characters unread.
agent_relevance: Closest published design to ours (generator, critic, controller), except our controller is plain code and not a learned gain signal.

source: Lu et al. (2024) LLM Discussion: enhancing the creativity of LLMs via discussion framework and role-play (COLM 2024)
finding: Three phases: initiation, discussion (diverge) over several rounds, final convergence round. Role-play personas added. Beats single agent, brainstorm-then-select and LLM Debate on LLM-judged Originality in 4 of 4 benchmarks and Elaboration in 3 of 4.
numbers: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125. Benchmarks: AUT, Instances, Similarities, Scientific. Human eval: 1,406 responses from 42 annotators; humans also rated it above baselines on Originality and Elaboration in 3 of 4 benchmarks.
limits: Table text came out garbled from the PDF, so per-benchmark means were not extracted. Single small model. Role personas conflict with our G4 (no persona voters on single-answer problems) but this is open-ended divergent work. LLM judge is the same family as the generator.
agent_relevance: Evidence that an explicit divergent phase then a converge phase lifts originality for a small model. Convergence is a fixed last-round instruction, switched by code.

source: Lu et al. (2024) LLM Discussion (judge reliability)
finding: LLM judge agreed with mean human rating about as well as humans agree with each other. Humans favoured longer answers; the LLM judge did less so on Elaboration.
numbers: Kendall tau LLM vs mean human: Originality 0.5213, Elaboration 0.2753, Fluency 0.6017, Flexibility 0.5508. Human vs mean of other humans: 0.5094, 0.4753, 0.3692, 0.2071. One answer scored 1 by the LLM judge on Elaboration and 3.88 on average by ten humans.
limits: Judge was gpt-3.5, like the generator.
agent_relevance: Length bias runs in humans too. Length-normalise scores (G5).

source: Peeperkorn et al. (2024) Is temperature the creativity parameter of large language models?
finding: Temperature is a weak lever for creativity. Tested novelty, typicality, cohesion and coherence of stories at many temperatures.
numbers: Llama 2-Chat 70B (6-bit), minimal prompt. Temperatures .001, .334, .667, 1.0, 1.334, 1.667, 2.0; 100 stories per temperature for the diversity analysis. Weak positive correlation with novelty (one coefficient 0.730, SE .273), moderate negative correlation with coherence, none with cohesion or typicality.
limits: One model, one story prompt, simple task. Small human rating study.
agent_relevance: Do not use temperature as the generate-mode switch. Use structure (separate prompts, constraints removed) and code to pick.

source: Peeperkorn et al. (2024) framing: exploration needs control, not randomness
finding: Authors tie explorative creativity to Boden's conceptual spaces and argue creativity needs more deliberate control than randomness.
numbers: Qualitative.
limits: Position part of the paper.
agent_relevance: Supports mode control by a program rather than by a sampling dial.

source: TinyTim (2025) A family of language models for divergent generation
finding: TinyLlama-1.1B fine-tuned on Finnegans Wake as a pure divergent generator. Authors cast ordinary instruction-tuned LLMs as convergent evaluators and propose pairing the two.
numbers: Hapax ratio 0.643 vs 0.413 (gpt-5-mini); Yule's K 208 vs 47; 10 prompts; 2,400 samples generated, 1,013 kept; unique-word ratio vs token diversity r = -0.807. Kruskal-Wallis p<.0001.
limits: Group sizes in paper do not add up. No human novelty or usefulness ratings. Dual-process is a framing, not tested.
agent_relevance: A divergent specialist plus a convergent chooser is a testable split. Raw weirdness metrics do not show usefulness.

source: Suzuki & Banaei-Kashani (2025) Universe of Thoughts
finding: Prompt pipelines for combinational, exploratory and transformative creative reasoning. Beat zero-shot, CoT, ToT and graph-of-thoughts on one task, not all.
numbers: GPT-4o backbone, Gemini 2.5 Pro judge at temp 0. Bridge task creativity: T-UoT 0.698 vs CoT 0.651, zero-shot 0.566, GPT-5 0.649. Electricity: T-UoT 0.526, DeepSeek V3.1 0.571. Society: DeepSeek V3.1 0.723 vs C-UoT 0.649. E-UoT society utility 0.280 with novelty 0.810.
limits: Self-built 3-task benchmark. Text says creativity is the sum of novelty and utility but tables show the mean. Only one judge. Claims of beating GPT-5 hold mainly on Bridge.
agent_relevance: Pushing novelty up costs utility; the evaluate step must gate on utility (a code-checked constraint).

source: CreativeDC (2025) Enhancing diversity of LLM-generated educational tasks
finding: Two-stage prompt: diverge on the theme alone with no judgement, then converge by picking one idea and tying it to the target concept. Roughly 1.6 times more distinct high-utility tasks than CoT or base.
numbers: Qwen3-235B-A22B, temp 1.0, 20 theme-concept pairs. Vendi score at K=50: about 12 distinct high-utility for CreativeDC vs about 8 for CoT and base (p<.001). Expert clusters about 16 vs 9. 3 experts, 6 tasks: novelty win rate 96.67% vs 3.33%; validity 1.00 vs 0.78; interestingness 0.81 vs 0.50.
limits: Tiny expert study (3 raters). Only intro programming. No ablation. Cites Wallas and Guilford, not dual-process.
agent_relevance: Same model, same temperature: separating diverge and converge into stages lifted diversity. Fits our code-switched mode design.

source: Reasoning beyond the obvious (2025) ConDiFi: divergent and convergent thinking in LLMs for financial scenarios
finding: Benchmark scores divergent (scenario generation) and convergent (MCQ) ability separately for 14 models. The two rankings differ.
numbers: Divergent overall: cohere_command_a 8.04, deepseek_r1 8.03, gpt4o 6.92, llama4_maverick 5.91. Convergent CCS on hardest set: llama4_maverick 72.32%, o1 71.41%, deepseek_r1 70.10%. Average CCS 85.45% to 65.61% across refinements. Richness vs Elaboration r max 0.237.
limits: GPT-4o judges divergent output. Output capped at 4,096 tokens. No prompt or temperature sweep. Last 31,927 characters unread.
agent_relevance: Strong convergent models are not the best divergent ones: use different calls or models per mode.

source: MUTATE and ReDNA (2026) Beyond one path: evaluating and enhancing divergent thinking in interactive LLM agents
finding: Agents under immediate pressure to converge fixate on the first action. ReDNA separates unconstrained divergent candidates from constrained convergent selection and beats Self-Refine and EscapeAgent.
numbers: 10 scenarios, 56 paths. Path discovery GPT-5.4 48.2% to 67.9%; Claude Sonnet 4.6 53.6% to 73.2%; Llama-4-Maverick 23.2% to 51.8%; Qwen3-235B 39.3% to 64.3%. Human average 79.9%. Self-Refine lowered Claude to 44.6%. Ablation (GPT-5.4): reflect only 58.9%; full ReDNA 67.9%. AUT transfer originality 2.91 to 3.77. Judge-human pairwise 0.8447, Pearson 0.5564 (Originality 0.4094).
limits: Only 10 scenarios; LLM judge. Claude originality fell 2.764 to 2.616 under ReDNA. Base values differ between tables. Last 48k characters unread.
agent_relevance: Closest direct test of code-separated diverge then converge inside an agent loop. Self-refine without separation can hurt.

source: Effect of idea elaboration on automatic assessment of idea originality (2026)
finding: LLM and fine-tuned raters of AUT originality are biased by elaboration. Agreement with trained humans is weak on mixed human and ChatGPT-4o responses.
numbers: 81 students, 4,813 AUT responses (3,548 ChatGPT-4o, 1,265 human), 2 human raters ICC .93. OCSAI vs humans r = .28 overall, .59 on human responses only. Among machine raters r = .61 to .77.
limits: Only AUT, Italian data, ChatGPT-4o at default sampling, elaboration explanation not tested directly.
agent_relevance: A model judge of novelty is unreliable on model text. Score novelty by code (embedding distance from a pool).

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: open-ended homogeneity of language models (NeurIPS 2025 oral)
finding: Open-ended answers from many LLMs are alike within and across models. Changing decoding barely breaks this.
numbers: 70+ models; 100 queries (Infinity-Chat100), 50 responses each. At top-p 0.9, t 1.0, 79% of cases have mean within-model similarity above 0.8. Min-p 0.1 at t 2.0: 61.2% of pairs above 0.8. Cross-model similarity 0.71 to 0.82 (DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82). 31,250 human annotations, 25 raters per item.
limits: Specific LM-judge correlations only in figures, not read. Last 64k characters unread.
agent_relevance: Many samples from one model are one voice (supports G4). A generate stage needs forced difference, not more draws.

source: Kumar et al. (2025) Human creativity in the age of LLMs (CHI 2025)
finding: Human study of LLM help. Direct idea lists did not leave lasting homogenization, but strategy lists lowered diversity later. LLM guidance on convergent RAT tasks lowered later accuracy.
numbers: Exp 1: 460 participants, 9,457 ideas; originality in test round H(2)=9.14, p=.010; strategies vs none p=.009; similarity strategies vs none p=.017. Exp 2: 640 participants, guidance vs none -10.6 points [-18.6, -2.7], p=.005; direct answer vs none p=.682.
limits: Five AUT objects; short lab exposure; guidance condition longer than answer condition. Last 20k characters unread.
agent_relevance: LLM scaffolds change what people do next; cross-mode help can shape later divergence.

source: Nair, Gizzi, Sinapov (2024) Creative problem solving in large language and vision models: what would it take?
finding: Position paper with a small experiment on repurposing objects. Notes LLMs fail 'discontinuous' tasks needing a Eureka step; appendix lists Guilford divergent-convergent and Wallas stages as models for ML.
numbers: Prompts with affordance and task info beat a plain prompt (figure only, numbers not extracted). Random baseline about 30%. CLIP-B-32 100% on the nominal (no creativity) test.
limits: Preliminary; a few CLIP and ViLT models; numbers read only partly.
agent_relevance: Hint-style injection (affordances) acts like a code-supplied generate-mode cue.

source: C2-Eval (2025) benchmark of convergent and divergent creativity in foundation models
finding: Benchmark scoring Usefulness, Originality, Surprise; splits convergent (constrained, e.g. code) from divergent (open, e.g. stories) regimes.
numbers: Abstract page only: no result numbers.
limits: Abstract read only.
agent_relevance: Suggests scoring mode outputs on different criteria: correctness first for convergent, novelty for divergent.

source: Helie & Sun (2010) Incubation, insight and creative problem solving: a unified theory and connectionist model
finding: EII theory in the CLARION architecture: explicit (rule) and implicit (associative) processes interact across Wallas' four stages. Matched human data on incubation, insight, overshadowing.
numbers: Secondary report: 5,000 simulated runs; correct 35.3% on first instance and 45.3% on second in a coin problem.
limits: Known only from search-result summaries, not opened. Numbers second-hand.
agent_relevance: The oldest runnable dual-process creativity system: an implicit generator with explicit checks. Same split as ours.

source: Scientific Reports (Dec 2025) GenAI vs human ideas on AUT and RAT
finding: Search summary only: average and best GenAI ideas were rated more original than human ideas on AUT, and GenAI also beat humans on a convergent test (RAT).
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not opened; exact title and URL unverified.
agent_relevance: Counterweight: do not assume LLMs lack divergent output; the gap is diversity and fit.

source: Brain alignment of creative thought vs chain-of-thought training (2026 preprint)
finding: Search summary: a reasoning-chain-trained variant moved away from the creative pattern in brain alignment.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not opened; single preprint; claim second-hand and URL match unverified.
agent_relevance: Reasoning-tuned models may be weaker generators; consider a non-reasoning call for generate mode.

source: Cross-study alignment of LLM and human originality ratings (2026)
finding: Search summary: LLM ratings were less sensitive to context than human ratings.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Another warning against model-judged novelty.

source: Beaty, Silvia, Nusbaum, Jauk, Benedek (2014) The roles of associative and executive processes in creative cognition
finding: Cited by Chen & Ding as the dual-process source: remote association plus executive inhibition. Human side belongs to the other angles.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Only seen as a citation.
agent_relevance: Gives the human template: associate, then inhibit.
